question: The Cabinet Mission sent to India in 1946 by the British Government comprised of ________ members.
solution:
The correct answer is __**three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Cabinet Mission was sent to India in 1946 by the British Government.
 
• The mission comprised three members: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander.
 
• Its primary aim was to discuss the transfer of power from British rule to Indian leadership.
 
• The mission also aimed to discuss the setup of a constituent assembly to draft the constitution of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Pethick-Lawrence**

 
 
• He was the Secretary of State for India and Burma at the time of the mission.
 
• He played a key role in the discussions regarding India's independence.
 
 
 
• **Sir Stafford Cripps**
 
 
• He was the President of the Board of Trade and had previously led the Cripps Mission in 1942.
 
• Cripps was known for his efforts to secure Indian cooperation during World War II.
 
 
 
• **A.V. Alexander**
 
 
• He was the First Lord of the Admiralty during the time of the mission.
 
• Alexander had a significant influence on British naval policies during and after World War II.
 
 
 
• **Cabinet Mission's Objectives**
 
 
• The mission sought to resolve the political deadlock between Indian leaders and the British government.
 
• It aimed to discuss the framework for the transfer of power and the future governance structure of India.
 
• The mission proposed a federal structure for India, which was later rejected by the Indian National Congress.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Cabinet Mission**
 
 
• The mission's proposals led to significant discussions and debates among Indian leaders.
 
• Though the mission did not achieve all its objectives, it paved the way for further negotiations.
 
• Ultimately, it contributed to the process leading to India's independence in 1947.
